title: Record detail header ignores `userActions.delete.visibleWhen` — the BOOLEAN form of the same key reaches all three delete surfaces, the predicate form only reaches the row kebab
body:
## Summary

`userActions.delete` reaches the record detail header in its **boolean** form but not in its **predicate** form. Same key, same button, two different scopes — and nothing warns the author.

* `userActions: { delete: false }` → Delete disappears from the row kebab, the selection bar **and** the detail header.
* `userActions: { delete: { visibleWhen: … } }` → the row kebab honours the predicate; the detail header keeps rendering Delete on records the predicate excludes.

So an author who upgrades from "nobody may delete this object" to "these rows may not be deleted" — the exact reason the object form exists — silently loses two of the three surfaces they had.

## Repro (framework `examples/app-showcase`, console at pinned `6314e87`, signed in as ADMIN so permissions are not a variable)

`showcase_invoice` already ships the declaration (`src/data/objects/invoice.object.ts:58`):

```ts
userActions: {
  edit:   { disabledWhen: P`record.status == 'paid'` },
  delete: { visibleWhen:  P`record.status != 'paid'` },
}
```

On a **paid** invoice (`INV-1011`, predicate false):

| surface | Delete |
| --- | --- |
| list row kebab | **hidden** ✅ (and Edit correctly renders greyed via `disabledWhen`) |
| record detail header `⋯` | **still offered** ❌ |
| selection bar with only that row ticked | **still offered** ❌ (filed separately) |

Control on a non-paid invoice (`INV-1001`, predicate true): Delete present on all three — so the absence above is the predicate, not a render failure.

Control on the boolean form — temporarily `delete: false`, artifact rebuilt:

```
{"form":"boolean false","rowDelete":0,"bulkDelete":0,"detailDelete":0}
```

All three gone. That asymmetry is the finding.

## Where it diverges

* Row kebab evaluates the predicates: `plugin-grid/src/components/RowActionMenu.tsx:299-301` → `isBuiltinRowActionVisible(input.deletePredicates, 'delete', row, scope, objectFields)`, fed by `resolveRowCrudAffordances` (`ObjectGrid.tsx:1659`). The child-row menu does the same in `plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx:1111-1112`.
* Detail header does not: `plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx:306-307` resolves
  `showDelete: gatedSchema.showDelete && objectAllowsDelete && canDeleteRecord` — bucket ∧ object affordance ∧ record writability. `userActionPredicates(objectSchema?.userActions?.delete)` is never called on this path, even though `RelatedList` in the same package already imports it.

The record is in hand on this surface and the CEL evaluator is already in context (the header renders `readonlyWhen`-driven field states from the same record), so the input the predicate needs is present.

## Why this is a defect and not "per spec"

The predicate block's doc-comment (`spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:1053-1070`) says "the **row's** button", which the current implementation matches literally. But the key it modifies is documented one level up as governing "the generic CRUD affordances that **the UI** surfaces" (`object.zod.ts:1410-1421`), and its boolean form demonstrably does reach all three. A key whose *scope shrinks when you add a predicate to it* is not something an author can predict, and the failure is silent — ADR-0078 (no silently-inert metadata) is the rule this lands on.

Consequence in practice: `visibleWhen` is advisory UI gating (the spec says so — enforcement stays with permissions/hooks), so a hidden-on-the-list record stays deletable from its own detail page. An author who tested the list believes it is gated.

## Suggested fix

Fold `userActionPredicates(objectSchema?.userActions?.delete / .edit)` into `DetailView`'s `showDelete` / `showEdit` the way `RelatedList` already does, evaluated against the open record. `disabledWhen` should map to a disabled header button for symmetry with the kebab.

## Related

* Selection-bar half, split out because it needs a semantics decision first: objectstack-ai/objectui#4420
* objectstack-ai/objectui#4296 — a different layer of the same surface (the row kebab ANDs only the OBJECT-level permission and ignores the record-level verdict).
